A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGST expression is not a reliable indicator of carcinogen exposure or of initiation, but is a reliable indicator of the development of AHFs.
single PGST-positive hepatic cells are the first morphologic manifestation of initiation and that the number of such hepatocytes is a sensitive and reliable measure of the number of initiated cells.
the single PGST-positive cell is a putative initiated hepatocyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the number of single cells expressing PGST is directly proportional to the number of preneoplasias expressing PGST, and that this relationship is maintained even in the presence of the tumor promoter phenobarbital.

we have shown that there is a dose response relationship between single PGST positive hepatocytes and altered hepatic flocks (AHF) and that this relationship is maintained over a 4 month period of observation.
the single PGST-positive hepatic cell is an important marker for the initiation stage in hepatocarcinogenesis.
